So...what's your favorite first person shooter single player experience in recent years?

That's an excellent question. I can think of many that are great, but didn't have a single-player campaign. Honestly the most recently single-player FPS game I played and enjoyed was Call of Duty: Black Ops 3's campaign. It was still very much your typical CoD campaign, but they made some good efforts to break out of the familiar corridor shooter and let you seize control of an area from multiple angles. The exo abilities and basic skill tree were a nice improvement since that's something I enjoy in the multiplayer, and the movement mechanic felt like it was lifted right out of Titanfall. I know most fans of CoD play it for its multiplayer or zombies, but I feel like for the first time in a while there was a worthwhile campaign gameplay experience there as well.

Metro 2033 and Metro: Last Light. The story kept me interested, the game play was varied enough to keep it fresh. I loved the weapons modification system. Voice actor was pretty good. And the atmosphere of the game as a whole was fantastic.

I also highly recommend the Metro games. I wasn't too fond of Last Light however, the stealth segments seemed to make the game far too easy.

I think the broken easy stealth had been added to the 2033 Redux, although I haven't played it myself, I played the original version.

I've actually really enjoyed the recently released Homefront: The Revolution. I'm in the process of reviewing it, but I think it got more hate than it deserved. I wouldn't say it was worth the release price entry fee, but if you get it for less than that (like I did), it's alright. It won't blow you out of the water, but it's a pretty solid game. Most of the hate seems to be directed at either the performance (which they've said they're addressing), or the premise of North Korea invading the US, which I don't have a major problem with - it's not trying to be hyper-realistic or anything.
Doom is the only correct answer. It is hands down the best SP campaign in a FPS in years.

• Borderlands

In BL1 the gun engine was, simply put, gorgeous. I loved the immersiveness and it really got me hooked on shoot-n-loot as a playstyle. The randomly generated enemy groups were especially nice, and one of the things I came back for again and again.

In BL2 we got to see them really push the envelope, I think the ratio of good to bad was about 50/50. Corporations' gun styles got more unique, but they also reduced the backpack size and added a new damage type (slag) for what appears no reason.

I have high hopes for BL3 - I'd like to see more of the open world ideas, like long-term hunting missions and more ridiculous guns, but I worry that they'll try to turn it into an FPS MOBA with a bunch of gimmicky abilities and a tiny sliver of elite guns that people farm for out of a massive pile of junk. We shall see.
